m.description: Number of distinct item sizes (item types)

b.description: Number of items (demand) required for each item type

assumptions.description: There is at least one item type.
Every item size is a positive integer that does not exceed the bin capacity.

code.python: assert all(1 <= w[d] <= W for d in range(m))

assumptions.description: The demand for every item type is positive.

code.python: assert all(b[d] >= 1 for d in range(m))

A.description: Arc set of the graph G=(V,A) on vertices V={0,...,W}: an item arc (i, i+w_d, d) for every item type d and start vertex i (tagged with type d), plus a loss arc (k, k+1, -1) for every k=0,...,W-1 (tagged with sentinel -1)
A.formulation: A = \{(i, i + w_d, d) : d \in \{0, \ldots, m-1\},\; 0 \leq i \leq W - w_d\} \cup \{(k, k+1, -1) : k \in \{0, \ldots, W-1\}\}

out.description: Adjacency list of outgoing arcs (arcs leaving each vertex)

inc.description: Adjacency list of incoming arcs (arcs entering each vertex)

D.description: Item arcs of each item type

x.description: Flow on arc (i,j): the number of items placed in any bin at a distance i from the beginning of the bin, on an arc of type d (or a loss arc if d = -1)
x.indices: (i, j, d) for (i, j, d) in A

z.description: Number of bins used (feedback arc flow from vertex W back to vertex 0)

constraints.description: Flow conservation at vertex 0: inflow minus outflow equals the negative of the number of bins used.

code.gurobipy:
model.addConstr(
    gp.quicksum(x[i, j, d] for (i, j, d) in inc[0])
    - gp.quicksum(x[i, j, d] for (i, j, d) in out[0])
    == -z
)

constraints.description: Flow conservation at every intermediate vertex: inflow equals outflow.
Flow conservation at vertex W: inflow minus outflow equals the number of bins used.

code.gurobipy:
model.addConstr(
    gp.quicksum(x[i, j, d] for (i, j, d) in inc[W])
    - gp.quicksum(x[i, j, d] for (i, j, d) in out[W])
    == z
)

constraints.description: The full demand of every item type must be packed.

code.gurobipy: model.addConstrs(x[i, j, d] >= 0 for (i, j, d) in A)

constraints.description: The number of bins used doesn't exceed the total number of items.

objective.description: Minimize the total number of bins used.

notes: This is the arc-flow MILP formulation based on Equations 7-11 of carvalho1999 (with one added bound on z, noted below). Arcs $(i,j)$ in the paper's graph $G=(V,A)$ are indexed here by a single index and tagged with the item type they represent (or -1 for a loss arc), analogous to how p9 (MCND) encodes arcs with `tail`/`head` arrays.

The paper writes the objective and vertex-0/vertex-W flow balance in terms of an explicit feedback arc $z = x_{W0}$; we instead treat z as a separate scalar variable equal to the number of bins used, which is equivalent and avoids adding a self-referential arc to A.
The paper's arc reduction criteria (Criteria 1-3) and valid inequalities (Propositions 2.2, 2.3) are solver-side optimizations, not part of the base formulation, and are excluded here.

This dataset's canonical problem-level parametrization for p22 is the individual-item list $(W, n, l)$ used by formulation `a`; `gen_params.py` derives $(m, w, b)$ by grouping items into distinct sizes (sorted in decreasing order, following the source's own convention of ordering items by decreasing width) and counting each size's multiplicity as its demand.

The bound $z \leq \sum_d b_d$ is not present in carvalho1999's Equations 7-11; it is added here because vertex 0 has no incoming arcs and vertex W has no outgoing arcs, so a pure-loss path $0 \to 1 \to \cdots \to W$ can carry arbitrarily large flow (and hence arbitrarily large z) while satisfying every other constraint, leaving z otherwise unbounded above. The bound never excludes an optimal solution, since an optimal packing never uses more bins than there are items. This mirrors the analogous total-usage bound added to formulation `b`.
